Entry Great Stallion of the Dothraki The Dothraki connect the world, the stars, and the future of their kind to the prophecies of the Great Stallion. For Khalasar, this is not book theology, but the universe of horses, blood, migration and glory. If outsiders only hear it as a barbaric slogan, they will not hear the meaning in it. Altars, relics, and prophecies can unite people and give a political claim the appearance of irrefutability.

Entry Great Stallion of the Dothraki The Dothraki connect the world, the stars, and the future of their kind to the prophecies of the Great Stallion. For Khalasar, this is not book theology, but the universe of horses, blood, migration and glory. If outsiders only hear it as a barbaric slogan, they will not hear the meaning in it. Some people use it as a talisman, while others use it as the name of fear; the same prayer may make people draw their swords or put them down.

Entry Great Stallion of the Dothraki The Dothraki connect the world, the stars, and the future of their kind to the prophecies of the Great Stallion. For Khalasar, this is not book theology, but the universe of horses, blood, migration and glory. If outsiders only hear it as a barbaric slogan, they will not hear the meaning in it. Whether the gods responded or not could not be proven by the account books, but how the rituals were held and who could interpret the omens actually determined the authority of the community.

For Khalasar, this is not book theology, but the universe of horses, blood, migration and glory. If outsiders only hear it as a barbaric slogan, they will not hear the meaning in it. They seek an explanation they can rely on when it comes to birth, marriage, sowing, illness, and death; the names of gods may not be the same, but their desire to keep their families safe is similar.
